title: Rule
description: One ruling, kept verbatim with its origin, scope, status, effective and expiry times, one rendered rule line and its attributed amendments, at pool/records/rule/<rule_id>.json. A temporary rule is this same record with an expiry time, a lift condition or both. See spec/pool.md, Rules.

task_id.description: Given when the rule is narrowed to one task generation, as a change that rides an Imperative revision is.

subject.description: What the rule governs, as a fixed key such as lane-limit, model-default or delivery-posture. Two rules in force on one subject at one scope are a conflict unless one of them names the other in changes.

words.description: The Hive Mind's exact words, or the request text as submitted. Never rewritten.

origin.description: Where the words came from: the intake receipt, session input, policy request or instruction, by reference, and the kind of source.

rule_line.description: The one rendered rule line: the operational interpretation of the words, supplied by the recorder, without its source suffix. The resolver appends the source and revision.

applies.description: Which roles the rule applies to. Empty means every role.

status.description: in-force, expired, lifted or ended. The resolver reads the clock as well: a rule in-force past its expiry time is excluded before its expiry receipt exists, and one that is not yet effective is excluded until it is. A supersession is never a status: it is read from the superseding rule's changes at each resolution.

expires_at.description: A temporary rule's expiry time. The resolver excludes the rule from this instant on, whether or not the expiry receipt has been written.

lift.description: A temporary rule's lift condition: the receipt kind and the record it must be about. The rule binds until the owner records the lift with that receipt as evidence.

changes.description: The standing rule this rule supersedes or qualifies, by identity and revision. That rule is never edited and nothing is recorded on it. The relation is read at each resolution: a superseded rule is excluded only while this rule is itself in force for the scope, the role and the instant resolved, so a temporary rule that expires, is lifted or is not yet effective leaves the standing rule in force. A qualifying rule and the rule it qualifies are both in force and are not a conflict, at one scope or across scopes: the narrower scope's rule does not override the rule it qualifies.

authority.description: The applying authority, with its intake receipt where the rule was applied by a request.

intake.description: The intake receipt of the request that applied the rule, where there is one.

amendments.description: Attributed revisions of the rule's operation, never of its words or dates: an extension, an early end, a lift, a supersession or a note. Each is appended.

expiry.description: Once the expiry was noticed and honoured: the receipt and the time it was recorded.

noticed_at.description: When the owning supervisor noticed the expiry, from the Shadow's wake. Lateness is this time against expires_at.

role.description: The roles the design resolves policy for: the Hive, Fleet supervisors, the eight dispatch classes, reviewers, fixers and validation steps.

kind.description: extend: a later expiry. end: an earlier end. lift: the lift condition was met. note: an attributed remark.

new_expires_at.description: For extend or end: the new expiry time. The original expires_at is never changed.

evidence.description: For a lift: the receipt the lift condition named.

resolved_rule.description: One rule as the resolver applies it: the rendered line with its source and revision appended, and why it applies.

line.description: The rule line followed by its source: the rule identity and record revision in brackets.

temporary.description: True when the rule carries an expiry time or a lift condition.

conflict.description: Two rules in force on one subject at one scope, neither naming the other in changes. An unresolved conflict holds the action that depends on the subject.
